podcast.title: Zero DB Initiative Signatory
podcast.body: Disturbed is among the artists who signed the Zero DB initiative, founded in 2008 as part of the charity Reprieve. This initiative advocates for governments to enforce the Convention Against Torture and other related treaties, and encourages condemnation of music as torture. "The Sinees include Tom Morello, average against the machine, members of REM, rise against Pearl Jam, Trent Reznor, Limp Biscuit, system of a down, disturbed the estate of Prince, the Chili Peppers, Eminem, Marilyn Manson, Neil Diamond, Dr. Dre, and a host of others."

xref.title: Fan Self-Stabbing on Stage – Los Angeles, July 27, 1986
xref.body: During a Cure concert in Los Angeles on July 27, 1986, attended by approximately 18,000 people, an audience member named John Morland — recently broken up with his girlfriend and severely depressed — jumped onto the stage, pulled out a knife, and began stabbing himself in what appeared to be some kind of final romantic gesture intended for his ex. Much of the crowd assumed the incident was part of the show and cheered him on. Security grabbed Morland before he could do serious damage; he survived. The incident profoundly disturbed the band. "Our crowd thought it was part of the show, so they cheered him on."

xref.title: Corey Taylor's Statement on Violence
xref.body: Following the 2008 school attack by Morné Harmse, who blamed Slipknot, vocalist Corey Taylor issued a statement expressing disturbance over the violence but disavowing responsibility. He affirmed the band's "very positive" message, which encourages fans to express themselves, stick together, and help each other, explicitly stating, "I'm not encouraging anybody to kill anyone." "Corey Taylor of Slipknot released this statement. Obviously, I'm disturbed by the fact that people were hurt and someone died. As far as my responsibility for that goes, it stops there, because I know our message is actually very positive. I'm not encouraging anybody to kill anyone. I encourage our fans to express themselves, to stick together and to help each other."

xref.title: Estate as Zero DB Initiative Signatory
xref.body: The estate of Prince is among the signatories of the Zero DB initiative, formed in 2008 by the charity Reprieve. This initiative encourages condemnation of music as torture and advocates for governments to enforce the Convention Against Torture and other treaties concerning prisoner treatment. "The Sinees include Tom Morello, average against the machine, members of REM, rise against Pearl Jam, Trent Reznor, Limp Biscuit, system of a down, disturbed the estate of Prince, the Chili Peppers, Eminem, Marilyn Manson, Neil Diamond, Dr. Dre, and a host of others."

xref.title: Richie Edwards' Disturbances
xref.body: Richie Edwards was described as the most extreme member of Manic Street Preachers, suffering from depression, anorexia, drug use, and bouts of self-mutilation, and was morbidly fascinated with Kurt Cobain's final days. "Richie was the most extreme member of the Manic Street Preachers. He was also quite disturbed and prone to depression and erexia, drug use and boats of self-mutilation. He was also morbidly fascinated with the last days of Kurt Cobain."
